keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Verden row). The infobox gives '1806: 730 km2' and '1806: 20,000' (population); the principality 'covered the eastern part of the present Verden district, plus the southern part of the Rotenburg district and parts of the Harburg and Heidekreis districts'. A 15.5 km circle at 9.30E 53.00N (about 750 km2) is a soft stand-in; Ottersberg and Achim are not on the page.

ledger.note: 1180: the Hochstift. Infobox 'Established: 1180'; 'When the old Duchy of Saxony was carved up in 1180'. The diocese was 'founded around 800 in Verden upon Aller'.

1195: Rotenburg. 'In 1195 Prince-Bishop Rudolph I founded the castle of Rotenburg upon Wümme'; the infobox gives Rotenburg as the residence of the prince-bishops since 1195 (Verden remained the seat of the chapter).

15 May 1648: secularised. Infobox 'Secularised as the Principality of Verden: 15 May 1648'; the Peace of Westphalia 'disestablished' the bishopric and 'a principality of the Empire was established that was ruled by the Swedish crown'.

sources.title: Prince-Bishopric of Verden
sources.note: Established 1180; Rotenburg 1195; Lutheran 1558-1568; Edict of Restitution 1630-1634; secularised 15 May 1648 to Sweden; disestablished 1712; area 730 km2.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Verden row.

SCOPE. 1180 to 15 May 1648 (infobox). After that: the Swedish Principality of Verden (to 1712, 'disestablished'), part of the Duchies of Bremen-Verden; the page does not date the Danish occupation or the 1715 Hanover purchase (the prince-archbishopric-of-bremen dossier of another part covers Bremen). Reformation: Lutheran from 1558, church ordinance of 1568 (Eberhard von Holle); a Catholic bishop returned in 1630 under the Edict of Restitution 'until 1634'.

SHAPE. Circle 15.5 km at 9.30E 53.00N, between Verden and Rotenburg, tuned to the page's 730 km2. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Verden', 'Rotenburg (Wumme)'.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new (the Bremen-Verden duchies are in the Bremen dossier's successors).
